title: Bake-off (validators): z-ai/glm-5.3-flash

conflicts: This flower draws consensus power, i.e. stake delegated to validators this epoch. Other kinds of power in the NEAR ecosystem include House of Stake voting power (veNEAR/locked NEAR) and token-ownership power of liquid-staking token holders; neither is drawn here.
inferred: That Figment operates both figment.poolv1.near and ledgerbyfigment.poolv1.near is inferred from their names, not verified.
That a big delegator can influence how its pool votes or behaves is inference; delegation records alone do not show control.

mappings.why: Side width bands compress the validator's share of current-epoch stake so the largest petals are readable without hiding the long tail.
Bar height is the square root of the validator's stake share this epoch: shorter paths exaggerate small holders less than a linear scale.
Colour marks the kind of account holding the stake seat (staking pool, liquid-staking contract, or unknown), so pools of different kinds are told apart.
Solid outline flags self-declared names from pool-details.near via NearBlocks or named .near account ids; dashed or no outline flags less-attributed accounts.

The question is who stands behind validators, so each pool's side is split into its delegations by backer class: other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups (sub-1,000 NEAR delegations folded per pool and class).
Petals run largest stake first, clockwise from the top, so rank order reads directly.

power_means.claim: Power in NEAR consensus is stake-weighted: a validator's share of current-epoch stake is its weight in block production, so the delegators behind each pool supply that power. The 371 validators held 593.4M NEAR of stake this epoch.
Stake is moderately concentrated: the top 10 validators hold about 36.2% of epoch stake, one-third of consensus weight needs only 9 validators, and HHI is 0.0215 with Gini 0.836 over validators.

interpretation.summary: This flower ranks NEAR mainnet's 371 validators by their current-epoch stake (593.4M NEAR) and splits each pool's side into backer classes: ordinary delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups. Consensus power here is stake-weighted, so the backers standing behind each pool are who supply that power. Top-10 validators hold 36.25% of stake and 9 validators reach a 33% threshold. Pool names are self-declared; addresses are accounts, not people.
unknowns: Liquid-staking contracts (Meta Pool, LiNEAR, ...) appear as backers, but their own token holders are not listed; that layer needs their contract state.
The 424 idle pools (no seat, no proposal) were not crawled for delegators, so their backers are missing, though they hold very little stake.
Lockup contracts (*.lockup.near) are marked as a class, but their owners were not resolved, so we cannot say who controls them.
Pool owners (get_owner_id) are included only as kind unknown, not attributed to named operators.
All pool identities are self-declared; none are verified.
Addresses are accounts, not people: we cannot tell which delegators are individuals, companies or bots.
